title: Continuous Batch Harmonizer and Attention Anticipator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce 99th/99.9th token latency for continuous streaming workloads by combining a low-friction admission smoother, batch-shape aware kernel probing, and an attention prefetch predictor. This ticket implements an end-to-end flow: (1) admission smoothing to avoid microbursts that amplify kernel warmup jitter; (2) a lightweight kernel-probing stage that measures effective throughput for the observed batch shape and sequence-length distribution; (3) an attention anticipator that prefetches KV-cache and warms attention kernels for likely continuation patterns. The design prioritizes minimal added latency on the fast path and graceful degradation under heavy load.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created initial RFC and measurement plan. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Continuous+Batch+Harmonizer+RFC

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype of admission smoother implemented in the local simulator. Early results: 15% drop in microburst-induced tail spikes for short (<40 token) sessions with mixed concurrency. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/feature/continuous-batch-harmonizer

2026-03-12 - Performance team (note): Kernel probing uses a two-tier probe window (fast 20ms probe, follow-up 100ms probe) to estimate kernel throughput without blocking the prefill path. Tradeoff: extra CPU sampling vs improved kernel fit. We agreed to keep probe CPU budget under 2% on the serving node.

2026-03-12 - Design feedback (R. Kim): Attention anticipator should be conservative for low-entropy prompts to avoid unnecessary KV prefetching. Suggested heuristic: only prefetch when continuation entropy < 3.5 (based on the eval set) or when previous decode repeatedly sampled the same attention span.

2026-03-13 - Liam O'Connor: Added canary rollout plan. Steps: unit tests -> integration tests on canary shard -> runtime perf A/B with 10% traffic -> 50% -> full. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/tail-latency?orgId=1&var-env=canary

2026-03-13 - QA (M. Hernandez): Need a regression test for worst-case with highly heterogeneous batch shapes (mix of single-token and long sequences). Creating synthetic workload generator ticket PM-9821 as dependency.
next_steps: Integrate attention anticipator with KV cache API (Aisha)
Run 48h canary to capture 99.9th metrics under production mix
acceptance_criteria: <10% increase in mean p50 latency on fast path
Reduce p99 token latency by >=12% on mixed-streaming workloads
Kernel-probe CPU budget <2% and network overhead <1%
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing existing global admission quotas; instead it smooths arrivals and improves kernel selection decisions. If canary results show regressive SLOs for any customer, rollback will be immediate and we will revert probe-enabled scheduling.
